retained_history.v: If $y = \log_2(\ln{x})$, what is $\dfrac{\textrm d y}{\textrm d x}$?

First, we express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y = \log_2 u, \qquad u = \ln x
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\dfrac{\textrm d y}{\textrm d u} = \dfrac{1}{u\ln 2}, \qquad \dfrac{\textrm d u}{\textrm d x} = \dfrac{1}{x}
$$

We now apply the chain rule, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{dy}{dx} &= \frac{1}{u\ln 2} \cdot \frac{1}{x} \\
&= \frac{1}{xu\ln 2} \\
&= \frac{1}{x\ln x\ln 2}
\end{aligned}
$$
